Import.PruneTooltip: When checked, manager-origin entities missing from this export are removed. Origin is decided by the import manifest recorded at each import (an id seen in a previous import is manager-origin); stores that predate the manifest fall back to campaignId classification, which is less reliable. Left unchecked (the default), missing entities are kept and listed in the report — a partial or hand-assembled export is indistinguishable from a manager-side deletion. Note an asymmetry independent of these toggles: body size always updates from the manager (an atlas-side size edit can be overwritten), while the atlas typeKey is never touched by a merge.

Off by default: unlike orbital motion, a turning sphere has to be pre-rendered frame by frame (about 2.4 MB of images per body, for the twelve largest bodies in a system), so this trades memory for a small amount of extra life. Turning it off frees that memory immediately. Per-player, and it obeys the pause switches above.

Foundry's grid: the image has no lines and Foundry draws its own, so you can change their colour and opacity per scene in Scene Configuration. The squares, walls and tokens line up the same either way. Applies when a battle map is built or regenerated; a regenerated map switches to the chosen grid once, then keeps your own opacity.

GalaxyNames.Hint: How system and sector names are drawn on the atlas window’s galaxy map. Auto draws names at a size you can read at any zoom, always naming the party’s system and the systems with missions, then as many others as fit without overlapping; zoom in for more. Map-scaled draws every name at map size, as before, so names are tiny when zoomed out. The default uses Auto on galaxies of up to 250 systems and Map-scaled on bigger ones, where Auto pans more slowly on integrated graphics. Per-player.
GalaxyNames.Name: Galaxy map names

HeroActorType.Hint: The Actor type content sync creates the Campaign Manager’s characters (heroes) as. Detected from the active game system the first time a hero is synced; change it here if the guess is wrong. Only affects Actors created after the change — an existing Actor keeps its type.
HeroActorType.Name: Actor type for synced heroes

ManagerCampaignId.Hint: The id of the manager campaign this world mirrors. Used for both the socket room and the import fetch.
ManagerCampaignId.Name: Campaign Manager campaign id

ManagerEnabled.Hint: Watch the Campaign Manager for galaxy map changes and light a badge when it has updates. Nothing is ever imported automatically — you still review and commit the merge. (Missions, journals and actors sync separately via IA-Companion.)
ManagerEnabled.Name: Sync Galaxy from Manager

ManagerToken.Hint: Paste a cmk_… API key minted in the Campaign Manager Dashboard (expand the campaign card, then Foundry API Keys → New key). It carries full GM rights on that campaign — treat it like your GM password — though it cannot manage other API keys. Stored on this client only — never synced to player clients. It does not expire unless you set an expiry, and revoking it in the manager cuts this bridge immediately, even on an already-open connection. A legacy GM login token still works here too, but expires daily. If the sync chip reports repeated disconnects, the key has probably been revoked.
ManagerToken.Name: Campaign Manager API key

ManagerUrl.Hint: Base URL of the Campaign Manager web app, e.g. https://manager.example.com. No trailing slash. Leave blank to disable the sync bridge.
ManagerUrl.Name: Campaign Manager URL

NpcActorType.Hint: The Actor type content sync creates the Campaign Manager’s NPCs as. Detected from the active game system the first time an NPC is synced; change it here if the guess is wrong. Only affects Actors created after the change — an existing Actor keeps its type.
NpcActorType.Name: Actor type for synced NPCs

PerfReadout.Hint: Shows frame-time figures on the planet globe and counts the atlas’s animation frames (run __iaPerf.report() in the browser console to read them). For diagnosing slow rendering — leave it off otherwise. Per-player.
PerfReadout.Name: Performance readout (diagnostic)

PoiAssetBasePath.Hint: Folder containing the ship / station / point-of-interest artwork, one file per kind ({kinds}). No trailing slash.
PoiAssetBasePath.Name: POI art base path

ShowLabels.Hint: Draw each planet, star and point of interest’s name on system scenes. Per-player.
ShowLabels.Name: Show body name labels

ShowMissionBadges.Hint: Draw a status icon on every body that has a mission pinned to it. Per-player.
ShowMissionBadges.Name: Show mission status badges

SiteAssetBasePath.Hint: Folder containing the surface-site artwork, one file per kind ({kinds}). No trailing slash.
SiteAssetBasePath.Name: Site art base path

ViewTilt.Hint: 0 = straight-down, 63 = angled orrery view matching the Campaign Manager. Animation applies this live; regenerate a system scene to redraw its orbit paths at the new tilt.
ViewTilt.Name: System view tilt (degrees)

WindowAnimation.Hint: Move planets, moons and stations in the atlas window’s system view. Per-player: turning it off holds this window still while the rest of the world keeps moving, so turning it back on catches the bodies up. To stop the orbits everywhere, for every client, use the world-level “Pause orbital animation” setting instead.
WindowAnimation.Name: Animate orbits in the atlas window

ZoomSpeed.Hint: How the atlas window moves between its views: opening a star system from the galaxy map, or a planet or moon from its system, zooms into it, and going back zooms out; a planet’s globe and its surface map cross-fade briefly. Quick suits a GM at the keyboard; the cinematic lengths are for a table screen. Per-player. Off switches instantly, and so does your operating system’s reduced-motion setting, which always wins.
ZoomSpeed.Name: Deep zoom (atlas window)

MissionObjectArt.Name: Mission object art folder
MissionObjectArt.Hint: A folder in your Foundry Data with your own token art for battle-map mission objects, matched by name: Terminal.png, Terminal_Red.png, Crate.png, Crate_Blue.png, Door.png (a bar across the wall, on a square canvas)… Anything missing keeps the painted token. Leave empty to use painted tokens only.

City.LayerUnreadable: This map’s building layer is in a shape the atlas does not recognise — the eraser, stamp and road tools are unavailable for it.
City.ReadOnlyViewOfSettlement: {reason} — read-only view of {name}'s Campaign Manager city map.
City.DetailFull: This town has the most painted items it can hold (2,500). Remove some first.

CityGenerate.AnchorsClassicOnly: Blended places quarters itself. Anchors are Classic only.
CityGenerate.CompassMoveNote: Changing a quarter's compass moves its graft the way a Reroll does — existing quarter districts keep their old outlines. The anchor steers the search; the quarter still lands on the nearest edge slot that clears the civic core.
CityGenerate.DetailEditedNote: You have edited the painted map’s detail by hand (removed, moved, added or given it artwork). Regenerating rolls new detail and replaces those edits.
CityGenerate.GreyedQuarterNote: A greyed quarter is one this settlement already is — a garrison inside a GARRISON. Every other kind grafts onto every base.
CityGenerate.GreyedQuarterShort: A greyed quarter is one this settlement already is.
CityGenerate.MatchTerrainClassic: Stored with the city. The classic layout reads none of it yet — switch to Blended to see it.
CityGenerate.MatchTerrainOff: Off — this city is generated from its seed alone, exactly as it would have been before the terrain knew where it was.
CityGenerate.MatchTerrainOn: The settlement’s own ground steers the plan, cuts the map at the shore, and names what it finds.
CityGenerate.NoArchetype: No archetype — this settlement type alone picks the base layout.
CityGenerate.PlanWheelOnly: Classic always uses the wheel plan.
CityGenerate.PresetsApplyToClassic: Presets apply to the classic layout.
CityGenerate.ReplacesLayerNote: Replaces the building and road layer, including anything stamped or drawn by hand. Districts and points of interest are left alone.
CityGenerate.RerollMovesQuartersNote: Reroll moves the quarters; existing quarter districts keep their old outlines — delete them first for a clean reroll.
CityGenerate.StyleHint: How the town is built on the painted map. Auto: delved in cavern towns, adobe on desert worlds, industrial on frozen ones, airless on airless worlds, classic elsewhere. Airless (hab domes joined by tubes) and Delved (pods, mining prefab, ore-cart rails and pillar towers) may be picked on any world; the ground and the light stay the world’s. A garrison, spaceport or works stays industrial whatever you pick.
CityGenerate.StyleNext: Takes effect on the next Generate.
CityGenerate.PadLookHint: Auto gives an open world’s landing pads the painted circle, the ferrocrete pad and the gantry cradle. Sunken docking bays sinks the medium pads and the bays in round walled pits instead; small pads stay painted. A garrison’s pads keep their blast walls, and a harbour town its stilts, either way.
CityGenerate.PadLookNext: Takes effect on the next Generate.

Tier.FinishOrCancelShapeFirst: Finish or cancel the shape edit first

Fog.PlayerNote: Players see concealed ground as blank board and cannot open a settlement under it. You always see the whole map — concealed ground is hatched.

SurfaceGenerate.SeedNote: Regenerate keeps this world’s seed — same landmass, new dials. Reroll draws a different world.

Status.Ready: Protected. This browser holds the GM key.

GmKey.ProtectHint: Protecting seals the GM galaxy with a key only GM browsers hold; players get a copy with only what they may see.
GmKey.ShareHint: Give this key to any other GM or Assistant GM, by hand: they enter it once on each browser they use.
GmKey.EnterHeading: Enter a key on this browser
GmKey.BackupHint: A plain JSON copy of the whole galaxy. Without the key the protected galaxy cannot be opened, so keep backups.

Upgrade.Intro: Campaign Atlas 0.4.0 keeps the GM's galaxy away from players. Until now every player's browser received the whole galaxy, hidden systems and notes included.
Upgrade.How: The GM galaxy will be sealed with this key, which only GM browsers hold. Save it somewhere safe (a password manager is ideal): without it the protected galaxy cannot be opened.
Upgrade.Backup: A backup of the galaxy downloads first. Older Atlas versions must not be used on this world afterwards.
Upgrade.SaveFirst: save the key first, then tick the box.
Upgrade.Done: the galaxy is protected. Players now receive only what they may see.

GmKey.Entered: the GM key opens the galaxy. Editing is back on this browser.
GmKey.NotAKey: that isn't a GM key (43 letters, digits, - and _).
GmKey.NotProtected: this world's galaxy isn't protected yet, so there is nothing to open.
GmKey.WrongKey: that key doesn't open this world's galaxy.
GmKey.ChangeConfirm: Make a new GM key? Every other GM browser will need the new key before it can edit again.
GmKey.Title: Campaign Atlas: GM key
GmKey.Changed: a new GM key is in use. Save it and give it to the other GMs.
GmKey.ChangeFailed: the key couldn't be changed; the old one still works.
GmKey.MenuHint: The key that keeps the GM's galaxy away from players: show, copy, export, enter or change it, and back up the galaxy.

Chip.Title: This browser has no GM key (or the wrong one), so it shows the player copy and cannot edit. Click to enter the key.

Conditions.LocalNote: An Atlas-only body: its conditions are saved in the Atlas only.
Conditions.OfflineNote: This body’s conditions live in the Campaign Manager. They can be edited again when it is connected.
